title: Florence Pugh Hails Robert Pattinson’s Bond Role, Calls Him “No. 1 Vote” in Her Home
body:
Florence Pugh has publicly cheered the news that her “Dune” co‑star Robert Pattinson will step into the iconic role of James Bond, saying the actor has been “the No. 1 vote in my household” when it comes to the next 007. The actress, who will appear alongside Pattinson in the forthcoming *Dune: Part Three*, also hinted that she has quietly floated the idea of joining the Bond franchise herself, proposing the possibility to director Denis Villeneuve during their ongoing collaboration.

Pugh’s endorsement comes at a moment when the future of the Bond franchise is under intense speculation. After Daniel Craig’s departure, the mantle has been passed to several high‑profile names, but none have been confirmed as the next official 007. Pattinson’s casting, first announced in early 2024, was met with a mix of excitement and caution, given his reputation for taking on complex, brooding characters. Pugh’s enthusiastic remarks could help sway public sentiment, positioning Pattinson as a fresh yet credible choice for the British spy.

The actress’s comments also underscore the growing synergy between the *Dune* universe and the Bond series, both now under Villeneuve’s direction. Villeneuve, celebrated for his visually striking, character‑driven storytelling, is steering *Dune: Part Three* toward a climactic conclusion while simultaneously shaping the tone of the upcoming Bond film. Pugh’s claim that she has “pitched” a potential role to Villeneuve suggests that the director may be considering a more interconnected casting strategy, possibly weaving talent across his two high‑budget franchises. If Pugh were to join the Bond world, it would mark a notable crossover, echoing past instances where actors have transitioned between major franchises under a single visionary filmmaker.

Industry insiders note that Pugh’s rising star power—bolstered by acclaimed performances in *Midsommar*, *Little Women* and the recent *Oppenheimer*—makes her a valuable asset for any blockbuster. Her involvement could signal a shift toward more gender‑balanced casting in the traditionally male‑dominated spy series, a trend already hinted at by recent discussions about diversifying the Bond lineup. While no official talks have been confirmed, Pugh’s off‑hand remark may be a strategic move to keep the conversation alive and gauge fan reaction before any formal negotiations begin.

Fans have responded enthusiastically on social media, with many praising the chemistry between Pugh and Pattinson in *Dune* and expressing optimism that their on‑screen rapport could translate to a dynamic Bond partnership. Critics, however, caution that the chemistry that works in a science‑fiction epic does not automatically guarantee success in the distinct tonal world of a Bond thriller. The upcoming release of *Dune: Part Three* will be a litmus test for both actors’ ability to carry large‑scale, franchise‑defining projects.

As production ramps up for both *Dune: Part Three* and the next Bond installment, the entertainment industry will be watching closely to see whether Pugh’s playful suggestion evolves into an official casting decision. Should Villeneuve decide to integrate her into the 007 universe, it could herald a new era of cross‑franchise collaboration and broaden the narrative possibilities for the legendary spy. For now, the buzz surrounding Pattinson’s debut and Pugh’s endorsement adds a fresh layer of anticipation to two of cinema’s most eagerly awaited releases.
